text:
alex: quick RFC follow-up — i prototyped planar vs interleaved (packed) QKV layouts for MHA. sharing numbers + tradeoffs.

maria: post the bench numbers pls.

alex: bench on A100, fp16-like kernel stack. workload: B=8, heads=16, head_dim=64.
S=32: planar (B,S,H,D) ~ 11.7ms, packed QKV (B,3,H,D contiguous) ~ 12.8ms.
S=128: planar ~ 28.4ms, packed ~ 26.1ms.
S=512: planar ~ 95ms, packed ~ 82ms.

drew: interesting — planar wins at small S, packed wins at long S. intuition?

alex: yeah. planar gives contiguous head inner dims -> better L2 reuse for short sequences and for fused attention that scans small tokens. packed reduces global working set and simplifies KV cache layout for long sequences -> fewer strided writes, better throughput when seq grows.

tiffany: what about stepwise decode (S=1 append)? packed seems attractive. any overhead for rotary, scaling, or other per-head ops?

alex: rotary is contiguous on head_dim, so planar makes applying rotary slightly simpler (no view/copy). packed needs a small temp view or a strided kernel to apply rotary per-head. that cost is amortized for long seq. but for step decode the extra copy can spike tail latency.

sam: from runtime perspective we already select kernels by seq_len and head_dim. adding layout selection multiplies kernel variants. we need selector rules + cost model.

maria: what's the KV cache implication? decode path is sensitive.

alex: packed QKV -> KV cache append is contiguous per-step, so single memcpy/append. planar -> you must scatter per-head into the cache which becomes many small writes and causes latency jitter on slow PCIe/NVLink topologies.

drew: how about memory alignment and padding? did you test different paddings?

alex: yes. aligning head_dim to multiples of 16/32 helps tensor-core kernels. 128B alignment on base allocation improves cudaMemcpy throughput. packed layout benefits more from pad because contiguous writes scale better.

tiffany: proposal idea: default policies:
- decode (autoregressive) path: packed QKV by default to minimize per-step copies and simplify KV cache.
- encode/batch-heavy path: planar for short sequences to exploit head-level locality.
Add a cost-model gated selector to override.

sam: ops-bot: will add perf canaries for S in {1,8,32,128,512} and head_dim in {32,64,128}.

maria: fallback rules: avoid copies when head_dim % 16 != 0 by choosing unfused kernel that consumes planar layout directly. we should not copy to satisfy a fused kernel unless latency benefit > X ms.

drew: also test multi-query and uneven head dims (per-group head dims) — packed layout assumptions break there.

alex: agreed. i'll draft an RFC addendum with: perf table, selector pseudocode, kernel naming convention (mha.packed.fused, mha.planar.fused, mha.planar.unfused), and a matrix of when to prefer each.

tiffany: add a short decoding microbenchmark for private/on-prem where memcpy cost may be higher.

sam: :thumbsup: i'll instrument the canaries and add alerts if selector picks a non-default too often.

alex: quick pseudocode for transform we used (planar <-> packed):
```
# planar: (B, S, H, D) -> packed: (B, 3, H, D) contiguous over channel=3
x = x.view(B, S, 3, H, D)  # if already split QKV axis
x = x.permute(0,2,1,3,4).contiguous()  # now (B,3,S,H,D) then reshape to (B,3,H,S*D) if needed
# for decoders we keep (B,3,H,D) and append to KV cache per-step as contiguous chunk
```

maria: lgtm. keep it short in RFC, include the perf numbers and margin for copy cost.

drew: one more note: quantized kernels (int8) have stricter alignment and chunking; packed layout tends to integrate better with per-channel scale storage. document that.

alex: thanks. i'll open the RFC draft and tag y'all.

ops-bot: perf-canary created: bench/eng-runtime/mha/layout-selector/{S_head_dim_matrix}
